messages:
ivy: Heads-up — started seeing a few OOMs during a high-concurrency batch storm after the latest kernel selection tweak. Not full host OOMs, but per-process KV cache allocation spikes and then admission starts dropping requests.
sam: Can you paste the stacktrace / pprof link? Is this happening on the new int8 kernel path or the fallback fp16? :thinking:
ijordan: perf-bot uploaded a heap profile: https://perf.internal/pprof/2064123456/heap.html
perf-bot: alert: kv_cache_memory_pressure spike at 2026-10-03T15:12:34Z, 87% utilization, eviction rate increased x3 :warning:
ivy: pprof shows a big growth in KVCache::reserve() on the new fused-kernel. Heap diff attached:
```
- before: kv_cache_total = 48GB
- after: kv_cache_total = 62GB
hot path: kernel_fused_dispatch -> allocate_kv_slot -> KVCache::reserve
```
maria: latency regressed by ~12% on tail? Are we also seeing batch sizes increase during the storm (i.e., admission allowed bigger batches)?
sam: yes — admission logic allowed larger token budgets because kernel selection lowered per-token CPU time estimate. So batcher thought it could fit more tokens and pushed through, but KV footprint per token changed (fused kernel uses bigger KV shims). Mismatch between kernel memory model and admission budget.
ijordan: proposed quick mitigation: cap max tokens per-batch for nodes with >75% KV utilization. Add a soft-shedder that rejects new requests with `retry_after` when kv_util > watermark.
ivy: can we do a short-term config change instead of rewiring admission? Maybe reduce `batch_token_target` by 20% across the fleet for fused-kernel models.
sam: good quick fix. Also adding an eviction-aware admission: when eviction rate > 0.5/s, reduce admission by min(25%, (eviction_rate*10)% ) — simple heuristic.
maria: need to watch latency regression — lower batch_token_target will increase P50, we should route only background traffic to the throttled config. @sam can you make a ramp plan?
sam: I'll push a canary: decrease batch_token_target on 3 nodes in ashburn, observe KV util and tail latency for 30m. If stable, ramp to 20% nodes, then fleet. Will also add extra logging: `kv_util`, `eviction_rate`, `admission_decision` in the batch debug trace.
ijordan: longer-term: we should sync kernel memory accounting with our admission estimator. Two ideas: 1) per-kernel memory-per-token samples emitted at model load time, 2) maintain a rolling estimator keyed by (model_variant,kernel) with EWMA. That will let admission predict KV pressure correctly.
ivy: agreed. For the immediate thread: sam, do the canary and post the results here. Also tag infra on-call if we see host-level pressure. :thumbsup:
